title: Microsoft Agent 365: the control plane for agents

reasons: published before the check existed: kept live with a notice while a corrected version is prepared

summary: Hold: the Conditional Access instructions use the wrong policy condition, and the sign-in query omits a required filter for service-principal events. The briefing also overstates what blocking and registry coverage guarantee, and needs clearer licensing, government-cloud and preview qualifications.

claims.fix: Remove the blanket shutdown guarantee. Explain the platform-dependent effect of catalog blocking. claims.claim: The Conditional Access blocking path includes Users, agents or workload identities > Agents > All agent identities > Block.
claims.quote: Under Assignments, select Users, agents or workload identities. ... Under Include, select All agent identities ... Under Target resources ... All resources ... Under Access controls > Grant. ... Select Block.
claims.fix: Use 'Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies > New policy > Assignments > Users, agents or workload identities > Include > All agent identities'; then explicitly set Target resources > Resources (formerly cloud apps) > Include > All resources and Access controls > Grant > Block. Remove the invented Agents step; describe Report-only evaluation and subsequent enforcement separately.

claims.claim: POST /identity/conditionalAccess/policies with agent identities as the users condition implements the all-agent-identities blocking policy.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/identity/conditionalAccess/policies ... "clientApplications": { "includeAgentIdServicePrincipals": [ "All" ]
claims.fix: Use POST /beta/identity/conditionalAccess/policies with conditions.clientApplications.includeAgentIdServicePrincipals=['All'], conditions.applications.includeApplications=['All'] and grantControls.builtInControls=['block']. The users condition is for the separate agent-user-account policy. Explain that enabledForReportingButNotEnforced only evaluates and does not block.

claims.claim: Applying these Conditional Access policies requires Microsoft Entra ID P1.
claims.quote: Applying Conditional Access policies in your tenant requires the Microsoft Entra ID P1 license.
claims.fix: Keep P1, but also report https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/fundamentals/licensing#microsoft-entra-agent-id, which states that extending Entra security features to agents requires Agent 365. Distinguish the base Conditional Access prerequisite from Agent 365 entitlement.

claims.claim: Agent identity inventory and access to an identity's logs are available through Entra ID > Agents > Agent identities.

claims.claim: GET /beta/auditLogs/signIns?$filter=agent/agentType eq 'AgentIdentity' retrieves agent identity sign-in events.
claims.quote: Only interactive sign-ins are returned through GET signins API requests unless you set an explicit filter on the signInEventType property
claims.fix: Use the full documented request from the cited manage-agent-identities-admin page: GET /beta/auditLogs/signIns?$filter=signInEventTypes/any(t: t eq 'servicePrincipal') and agent/agentType eq 'AgentIdentity'. Mark it beta.
